pages.text: Icicles hung from the roof edge. The three walked beneath them to play in the snowy yard.
Kiki wanted to play all day. But after a quarrel with Nono, Kiki would not speak.
Kiki took off the gloves and played with bare hands.
"Are your hands cold?" Nono asked. Kiki lowered the head.
Kiki kept playing in the snow. The fingers went numb.
The stiff fingers could not make snowballs. The snow fell apart.
Kiki tucked both hands under the arms and curled up. There was no more playing.
Grandpa Badger said, "The longer you put up with the cold, the colder you get."
"My hands are cold," Kiki said. Grandpa brought a warm, damp cloth.
Kiki's hands softened again. With gloves on, Kiki played until evening.
